questions.stemHtml: In transverse spinal cord sections, cervical segments appear large and oval with prominent anterior horns (especially at C5–C8) due to upper limb innervation. Thoracic segments are smaller and rounder, with slender gray matter and a visible lateral horn (T1–L2) for sympathetic output. Lumbar segments are larger again, with broad ventral and dorsal horns to supply the lower limbs. Sacral segments are small and round, with thick gray matter and minimal white matter. Segment identification relies on size, shape, gray-to-white matter ratio, and horn prominence. Identify the spinal segment
